body.statement: Under complete randomization, every realizable completion \(T\in\mathcal S_N(F)\) with average squared contrast \(t\) satisfies \(\operatorname{Var}_Z(\widehat\theta_N)=[B_N(F)-t]/(N-1)\). Consequently the sharp marginal-information upper endpoint is \(U_N(F)\), and \(U_{\mathrm{lo}}(F)\le U_N(F)\le U_{\mathrm{hi}}(F)\) with computable width \([C_{\mathrm{alg}}(F)-V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)]/(N-1)\le3456/[N(N-1)]\). The fractional endpoint of Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025) is therefore an upper certificate for, but need not be representable by, an \(N\)-unit science table. The lower variance endpoint is exactly \(L_N(F)\), because the comonotone rank pairing attains \(C_{\max}(F)\) as both a fractional and realizable coupling.
body.justification: The theorem converts the transport integrality gap into a two-sided numerical certificate around the sharp upper variance endpoint without mislabeling it as a bound on the unknown actual completion.
body.gap: Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025) use fractional transport, and Brennan et al. (2025) use an integer program; neither supplies a universal analytic width connecting the two endpoints for the same empirical marginals.
body.consumer: Three-arm contrasts reported in trials such as ACTG 175 can pair an attainable completion with a fractional dual bound and report the exact remaining realization width.
